name: @tangram/ai
//: docs/plans/wave-zero.md §5's deliverable 5 — the provider contract, grounding, the prompts, the cache key and data.md D3's retrieve.ts, shared by apps/app and (from backend.md B1) apps/server. The eleven modules moved here from apps/app/lib/ai/** in one commit with their 66 import sites; `apps/app/lib/ai/` is now empty and backend.md B2's browser-side ask-client.ts is the only thing that goes back into it. The exports map gains a `./*` wildcard and KEEPS `.` pointing at schemas.ts: the frozen ask contract is what a server consumer means by a bare `@tangram/ai`, index.ts does not re-export it, and repointing `.` at the barrel would have changed the meaning of an import nothing in the tree has written yet. TWO DEBTS, BOTH RECORDED IN HANDOFF.md. The first predates this package; the SECOND IS THIS MOVE'S OWN — before it, packages/ai held only the import-free schemas.ts and depended on nothing. (1) THE EXPORTS MAP POINTS AT TYPESCRIPT SOURCE: these modules export runtime values and apps/server emits plain JavaScript that plain `node` loads. Node's type stripping handles the .ts itself today only because pnpm symlinks a workspace package and node's realpath lands outside node_modules; against a deploy artifact where @tangram/ai is a real directory under node_modules the same emitted dist/index.js fails with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING. And plain `node` does not get that far for ten of the twelve modules anyway: the intra-package imports are spelled ./x.js, the resolver does not substitute .ts for a .js specifier with no file behind it, and only deadline.ts and schemas.ts (which import nothing) load. The .js spelling is deliberate and is not the regression it looks like — extensionless ./x, which is what the move first wrote, is unresolvable in ESM too AND unresolvable under apps/server's nodenext typecheck, while ./x.js is what a real emit needs and is what lets tsc resolve the package under bundler and nodenext alike. Whoever needs the server to load this package must add a build emitting dist/*.js + .d.ts and point exports at {types, import}. (2) THIS PACKAGE IS NOT YET SELF-CONTAINED, though backend.md B1 made it much closer and this paragraph is its update. It read `@/lib/**` out of apps/app across eight app modules, SIX of them runtime values; B1 removed the lib/db half by MOVING the six browser-side known-set functions out of examples.ts into apps/app/lib/srs/known-set.ts (wave-zero.md §5's own rule: this package holds what the app and the server BOTH need, and the server resolves nothing out of Dexie). So a search for `lib/db` under `packages/` is now prose only and B1's criterion — 'packages/ai depends on zod, the SDK and lib/types.ts and on nothing under lib/db' — holds exactly. WHAT IS LEFT: ten `import type` edges (erased at emit) plus TWO runtime ones — sha1Hex from @/lib/dev/sha1 in cache-key.ts, and hasCjk from @/lib/dict/rank in retrieve.ts. Both are pure leaf functions with nothing under lib/db in their graphs, and both files are data.md D3's rather than B1's. This note previously said B1's ruling 'has to cover cache-key.ts and retrieve.ts too before apps/server can import anything here'; it did not have to, because apps/server bundles with esbuild and its build resolves `@/*` into apps/app (apps/server/scripts/build.ts). That bundle also settles debt (1) FOR THE SERVER — dist/index.js inlines this package, so no type stripping happens at all — while leaving it open for any other consumer. The `@/*` mapping in tsconfig.json is what makes the package typecheck in the meantime, and it is still a debt, not a design. BACKEND.MD B2 HALVED IT: the contract flip took retrieve.ts out of the server's graph (routes/ask.ts no longer retrieves), so the server's module graph reaches exactly ONE runtime app edge now — sha1Hex from @/lib/dev/sha1 in cache-key.ts, which routes/ask.ts and routes/examples.ts reach for the two prompt versions. Closing that one would let the mapping go for the server; `hasCjk` in retrieve.ts is the app's and the phones', not the server's. B2 also CLEARED THE 23 `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` ERRORS in ground.ts (18), fake.ts (3) and prompts.ts (2), and turned the flag back on in apps/server/tsconfig.json — which compiles every module of this package the server imports, so those are checked under it now. The flag is still off HERE, and the measured reason is 36 errors in apps/app/lib/dict/** (entries.ts 22, segment.ts 9, rank.ts 5) reached through retrieve.ts, which is data.md's code and was not B2's to churn. retrieve.ts is therefore the one module of this package that no gate now checks under the flag.
